newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-REAL STAY TOP AS BARCELONA AND DEPORTIVO SLIP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-REAL STAY TOP AS BARCELONA AND DEPORTIVO SLIP.

text.p: Real Madrid stayed top of the Spanish first division on Wednesday after Barcelona could manage only a 1-1 draw at home to 10-man Tenerife and Deportivo Coruna were held by the same score by Rayo Vallecano.
After beating Espanyol 2-0 on Tuesday, Real have 14 points from six games, leading Barcelona on goal difference.
Betis, 1-0 winners at Hercules, are a point back in third place and Deportivo Coruna fourth, a further point behind.
Valencia saw their recent good run cut short at home by a 1-0 defeat by unfancied Logrones in which Brazilian striker Romario blasted a penalty over the bar.
Valencia fans, angry with their team, applauded the Logrones players off the pitch at the end of the game.

A 78th-minute goal from a corner by Romanian midfielder Gheorghe Popescu seemed to have given Barcelona three points in their game with Tenerife but just four minutes later Juanele Castano equalised with a header.
Barcelona had played the last 20 minutes against only 10 men after Tenerife's Alexis Suarez picked up his second yellow card for a foul on Frenchman Laurent Blanc.
Once again former England manager Bobby Robson's side failed to work well as a unit and gave goalscoring Brazilian Ronaldo little chance to show his form up front.
With Barcelona drawing, Deportivo Coruna could have gone top. But they too lost ground after being held 1-1 at home by struggling Rayo Vallecano.
Deportivo may face disciplinary action after the referee was hit by an object while leaving the pitch. A 16-year-old youth was arrested in connection with the offence.
Just two weeks ago Spanish authorities closed Sevilla's ground for a similar incident.
The referee in the Basque derby match also had to be escorted from the field under a hail of objects after Real Sociedad beat Athletic Bilbao 3-1 against the run of play.
Newly-promoted Extremadura came within five minutes of earning their first-ever point in the first division after equalising Racing Santander's opening goal.
But to the disappointment of home fans who are already staring relegation in the face, Racing struck again in the 85th minute to leave Extremadura with six straight defeats.
